Similarity results as a data frame (optionally saved to Excel)

Source: R/similarity.R
similarity_to_df.Rd

Turns the result of [doc_similarity()] into a data frame you can view, filter and save. Two layouts are available:

Usage

similarity_to_df(
  s,
  type = c("matrix", "pairs"),
  data = NULL,
  title = "title",
  digits = 3,
  cutoff = 0,
  xlsx = NULL
)

Arguments

s

A result from [doc_similarity()].

type

`"matrix"` (default) or `"pairs"`.

data

Optional: the data frame passed to [doc_similarity()]. If given, the `title` column is added (`title` in the matrix; `title_1` and `title_2` in the pairs).

title

Name of the title column in `data`.

digits

Decimal places to round the similarities to (default 3). Use `NULL` for no rounding.

cutoff

For `type = "pairs"` (and the pairs sheet in Excel): keep only pairs at or above this similarity (0 to 1). Default 0 keeps every pair.

xlsx

Optional path for an Excel file (e.g. `"~/Desktop/similarity.xlsx"`). A missing `.xlsx` ending is added. When given, the data frame is returned invisibly.

Value

A data frame. For `"matrix"`: `id` (plus `title`) and one column per reference. For `"pairs"`: `id_1`, `id_2`, `similarity` (plus `title_1`, `title_2`).

Details

* `type = "matrix"`: one row and one column per reference, with the cosine similarity in each cell (the table behind the heatmap). * `type = "pairs"`: one row per pair of references, most similar first, which is easier to sort, filter and scan.

If you give `xlsx`, an Excel workbook is written with **both** layouts, on sheets named `similarity_matrix` and `pairs`, whichever `type` you asked for.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "sample_abstracts.bib", package = "citelens")
refs <- bib_to_df(f)
s <- doc_similarity(refs)
head(similarity_to_df(s, "pairs", data = refs), 3)
#>    id_1  id_2 similarity                               title_1
#> 1 syn02 syn06      0.761        Predicting student persistence
#> 2 syn21 syn29      0.724 Assessment and accountability metrics
#> 3 syn04 syn05      0.702        Predicting student persistence
#>                                 title_2
#> 1     Advising and first-year retention
#> 2 Predictive models in higher education
#> 3     Advising and first-year retention
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
similarity_to_df(s, data = refs, xlsx = out)
#> Wrote the similarity matrix (30 x 30) and 435 pair(s) to /tmp/RtmpVZl12j/file1a067afd4764.xlsx
